recertified_from: 2026-08-11 (AC_DEC 10 -> 50; same design.json, same sizing, only the sweep density changed)
what: The expert topology ported to IHP SG13G2 and re-sized to spec. This is the yardstick every candidate is scored against; `scripts/baseline.py --check` re-runs the frozen deck and fails if any number below moves.
bias: one ideal reference current into a real n/p mirror; every bias device is an integer multiple of that unit (per side: 2 units at each biquad output => 8 nA total)
notes: |H| at 1 kHz is -48.43 dB against -48.16 dB of 4th-order Butterworth arithmetic.
IRN 0.5-200 Hz = 49.98 uVrms is THE NUMBER TO BEAT: the challenge is < 40 uVrms. (Certified 50.18 on the old 10 pts/decade grid; the -0.20 uV is the density change, not a design change.)

RE-CERTIFIED 2026-08-12 at AC_DEC = 50. Same design.json, same sizing, same lane -- only the sweep density moved, because 10 pts/decade steps over passband features. Every delta was within tolerance except fc (+0.37 Hz) and ph_max (+0.31 deg), both of which are the denser grid resolving the curve rather than the circuit moving.

HONEST FAILURE, surfaced by the denser grid: the reference's own S3 flatness clause does NOT hold. ripple_db = 0.2512 dB against a 0.2 dB bound, over dc..150 Hz. At 10 pts/decade the samples straddled the feature and it read as passing. The reference remains the yardstick -- it is not a solution, and it was already expected to fail S5 -- but it must NOT be described as 'on spec on every line except noise'. It is on spec on every line except noise AND passband flatness.
mono_db = 0.0227 dB: the reference is essentially monotone, which is why it looks right by eye despite the ripple number. Its flatness failure is a shallow one-sided droop, not a bump.
Total drawn capacitance is REPORTED, never specced.
Every number here was measured in THIS repo on the frozen deck above -- nothing is carried forward from the originating campaign.
